## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about this prophet. None is used in this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Dhul-Kifl is identified by later writers with different figures (among them one called Ezekiel in earlier scriptures). These identifications disagree and none is used.
- The only ayat in the inventory are 21:85-86 and 38:48; the draft is deliberately short, because the Quran says nothing more of him.
- A scholar should check that 'one of the patient' and 'one of the best' are the right renderings, and that 'admitted into His mercy' fits the verb.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Named among the patient and the best  (`#named-among-the-patient-and-the-best`)

Cited ayat: 21:85-86, 38:48

> **21:85** وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
>
> **21:86** وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

> **38:48** وَٱذْكُرْ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلْأَخْيَارِ

### Claims

**c1** (21:85): Dhul-Kifl is named together with Ismail and Idris, and each of them is described as one of the patient.

**c2** (21:86): God says that He admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous.

**c3** (38:48): Dhul-Kifl is named again, with Ismail and Alyasa, and each of them is described as one of the best.

### One-minute summary

Dhul-Kifl is named with Ismail and Idris, each of them one of the patient [c1]. God admitted them into His mercy [c2]. He is named again with Ismail and Alyasa as one of the best [c3].

### Complete story

Dhul-Kifl is named together with Ismail and Idris, and each of them is described as one of the patient [c1]. God says that He admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous [c2].

Dhul-Kifl is named again, with Ismail and Alyasa, and each of them is described as one of the best [c3].

### Deep study

The Quran names Dhul-Kifl in short lists [c1][c3]. One list ends with a double statement: they are among the patient [c1] and God admitted them into His mercy as righteous [c2]. The other list gives one description, among the best [c3].

### Kids mode

God named Dhul-Kifl with Ismail and Idris and said each of them was patient [c1]. God took them into His mercy [c2]. In another place God named him with Ismail and Alyasa and said each was among the best [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran can honour a person with a brief mention and a single quality, patience, and that this needs no story to explain it [c1]. Another is that the mention is joined to God's mercy [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: anything Dhul-Kifl did or said, where or when he lived, or to whom he was sent.
- Not established: whether the Quran calls him a prophet or a messenger. The verses name him in lists and describe him as patient, righteous and among the best, and do not give him either title.
- Not established: what the name refers to or why he is called by it.
- Not established: what he was patient in.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later writers named various figures as Dhul-Kifl, including some known from earlier scriptures, and disagreed about whether he was a prophet; none of these identifications is used here.
